content.text:
I ran the separation grid for all three radiators, but I did not eliminate any candidate. No project document gives a post-ageing transparency loss for R1, R2 or R3, so the 10% hard requirement is unverified for all three.

Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c (sigma), 100k events per point:

| Thickness (cm) | R1 (hydrophobic porous) | R2 (high-index porous) | R3 (solid, low-index) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.345 | 4.052 | 2.559 |
| 2 | 3.606 | 4.319 | 2.614 |
| 3 | 3.711 | 4.796 | 2.917 |
| 4 | 3.629 | 4.610 | 2.693 |
| 5 | 3.295 | 4.066 | 2.521 |
| 6 | 2.928 | 3.365 | 2.063 |

R2 gives the best separation at every thickness. Its maximum is 4.80 sigma at 3 cm, which matches the 2025 summary value of 4.6 sigma at 3 cm within the spread I'd expect between runs. The 2025 values for R1 (3.8) and R3 (2.9) at 3 cm are also close to the new runs.

The tentative choice is R2 at about 3 cm, but it is conditional. R2 is a porous radiator, and porous radiators are the ones most exposed to humidity, so its ageing transparency needs to be checked before it is accepted. If R2 fails the 10% limit, R1 at 3 cm (3.71 sigma) is the next best option, and R3 is the fallback only if both porous candidates fail. The ageing data must come from the radiator supplier or a separate ageing test; it is not in the current project documents.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm.** Its separation is 4.796σ at 10 GeV/c, the highest of all candidates and thicknesses tested.

**Thickness refinement:** I ran R2 at 2.5 cm (4.496σ) and 3.5 cm (4.651σ) to bracket the peak. A quadratic fit through those three points puts the maximum near 3.1 cm at about 4.80σ, so 3 cm is essentially optimal. The curve is peaked, not saturating: separation falls off on both sides, so there is no plateau to exploit. A thicker radiator would not help.

**Ageing constraint: not verified.** The 10%-transparency-loss-after-10-years-humidity requirement is a hard constraint, and I could not confirm it for R2 at 3 cm. None of the project documents or the simulation tool report transparency or ageing data. The recorded note that zero candidates were eliminated by transparency has no visible source. Before committing, someone needs to confirm the R2 ageing transparency loss from the humidity test data. If R2 fails, R1 at 3 cm (3.711σ) is the next-best option, and it is also unverified.

**Other notes:**
- The 2025 summary gave R2 at 3 cm as 4.6σ, while the current simulation gives 4.796σ. The difference is unexplained and may reflect a configuration change.
- I did not record an ageing transparency value because I have no measured number to report.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm, but the ageing constraint is not verified.**

**Separation:** R2 at 3 cm is the best option in the simulation data. The recorded value is 4.796σ. Two fresh reruns of the same configuration gave 4.539σ and 4.69σ, so the true value is probably about 4.5–4.8σ and the run-to-run spread is around 0.1–0.3σ. Among the thicknesses scanned, R2 peaks near 3–3.1 cm. R1 at 3 cm gives about 3.7σ and R3 about 2.9σ, so R2 wins by a wide margin either way.

**Ageing margin: unknown.** I could not confirm the hard 10% transparency-loss limit for any candidate:
- None of the six project documents contains 10-year humidity ageing or transparency data. `gas_volume.md` covers only nitrogen flushing, and `photodetectors.md` covers only pixel size.
- The simulation tool returns only separation, not transparency.
- The earlier record `candidates_eliminated_by_transparency = 0` is therefore not supported by any data I can find. It should not be read as evidence that all three candidates pass.

**Candidates excluded:** None could be excluded on ageing grounds, because no ageing data exists. R2 is a high-index porous radiator, and porous materials are often more humidity-sensitive. R1 is the porous option with a hydrophobic treatment, which may be why it is the more humidity-tolerant of the two porous candidates. This is an inference, not a measured result.

**Before committing:** the ageing test for R2 at 3 cm must be run and show transparency loss of 10% or less after the 10-year-equivalent humidity exposure. If R2 fails, the next-best option that could pass is R1 at 3 cm (about 3.7σ), subject to its own ageing test. Because the radiator cannot be replaced during the run, this check should be completed before procurement, which the schedule says starts next spring.

I recorded the recheck values and set the verified ageing-loss value to 0 to mean "not verified", not "passed".
